key_insight: Large language models trained with reinforcement learning can still be distracted by irrelevant prompt changes, but measuring and suppressing the most unstable token choices during decoding can improve reasoning accuracy. The paper shows that semifactual interventions expose where this sensitivity comes from and how to reduce it.
problem_solved: This paper addresses the brittleness of RLVR-trained LLMs, which may change their predictions when prompts are altered in ways that do not affect the underlying task or correct answer.
method: Apply semifactual prompt interventions that keep the core problem and answer unchanged while modifying irrelevant prompt features.
Measure token-level sensitivity to identify which candidate tokens exhibit the largest drift under these interventions.
Suppress high-drift token candidates during decoding to steer the model toward more stable reasoning outputs.
impact: For AI/ML practitioners, this offers a practical way to diagnose and reduce prompt sensitivity in reasoning models. It can improve robustness and accuracy without changing the task itself or retraining the full model.
